newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin moves from hospital to sanatorium.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin moves from hospital to sanatorium.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin has moved from hospital to a sanatorium where doctors say he can now do more work and be more physically active while getting ready for a heart operation, the presidential press office said on Monday.
A brief Kremlin statement said Yeltsin's doctors recommended the move to the Barvikha sanatorium near Moscow and felt that "The condition of the Russian president is quite satisfactory."
Yeltsin, 65, had been in the exclusive Central Clinical Hospital since September 13.

He spent three weeks in Barvikha during the summer and voted there in the second round of the presidential election on July 3, keeping the world's press waiting at the Moscow polling station where Kremlin leaders usually vote.
Aides said at the time that Yeltsin had a cold and was tired after a gruelling election campaign.
The president, breaking a long Kremlin habit of secrecy about the health of its leaders, then said on September 5 that he would have an operation to improve blood supply to his heart.
A Kremlin spokesman said Yeltsin's workload and the volume of his physical activity would be increased at the sanatorium. A number of meetings were planned this week.

He said the president arrived at Barvikha over the weekend and had met Igor Stroyev, chairman of the Federation Council upper house of parliament, there on Monday. Earlier on Monday, the Kremlin press office had said Yeltsin was still in hospital.
The spokesman said the timeframe to get the president ready for the operation would not be changed.
Doctors said late last month it would take six to 10 weeks to prepare the president for the operation, which will improve the blood supply to his heart.
Yeltsin had two heart attacks last year and doctors say he may have had a third between the two rounds of the presidential election.
